answer: A new identity must first wander through a probation lagoon of low-value tasks, and only after passing a reputation prism that splits genuine contributions from duplicated ones does it earn voting weight. Sybil resistance can be built by requiring each agent identity to lock a stake that decays unless it maintains a verifiable history of unique, peer-attested work. Duplicating identities then costs real stake plus lost reputation, making mass sockpuppetry economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0277's threat model.
